sets.setting: Rentals for a hybrid worker choosing between a downtown office and neighborhood life.
sets.design_notes: B versus F is a close commute-and-lease trade-off, while B versus D is a medium cost-and-space contrast. D creates clear easy pairs through its modernity and access; E gives the budget/quiet counterpoint, and C exchanges access for room and outdoor space.

sets.setting: Rental search for someone balancing university access, weekend hosting, and a calm home.
sets.design_notes: C and F are close efficiency-versus-space choices, and A versus E is a close access-versus-light trade-off. D creates an easy price/lease contrast; B is the quiet hosting option with a longer commute.

sets.setting: Homes for a couple deciding between a short commute, home working space, and outdoor living.
sets.design_notes: B and F are close quiet-space versus commute-modernity alternatives; D versus E is a medium flexibility/access trade-off. A offers an easy commute-focused contrast, while C trades almost all access and lease flexibility for family-scale room and outdoor space.

sets.setting: Rental options for a remote worker who still visits the city several times each week.
sets.design_notes: A and E are a close quiet/outdoor versus commute/area trade-off; C and E form a medium modernity-light versus room-outdoor pair. B versus D is an easy access-versus-quiet/budget contrast, and F is the spacious outdoor extreme.
